P.O. Box 10341
Van Nuys, CA 91410
Fax: 1-833-886-7956

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-3A565C0679-61883
Notice Date: 2026-08-09
Requested Service: Lumbar fusion, CPT 22612
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-05

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for lumbar (lower back) fusion, CPT 22612, as described in your Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that you reverse this determination based on the records summarized below, which are enclosed.

**Disclosure regarding the criteria cited in this letter**

I understand that Iowa Total Care/Ambetter Health delegates prior-authorization review of musculoskeletal spine surgery, including lumbar fusion, to Evolent Specialty Services (formerly National Imaging Associates), and that Evolent applies its "Lumbar Spine Surgery" clinical guideline (identified in the documents I was able to obtain as Evolent_CG_1766, and in an earlier edition as NIA_CG_304) to CPT 22612. Iowa Total Care has not published a copy of this guideline on its own website, so I have not been able to confirm that the specific edition quoted below is the exact version applied to my request. The language quoted in this letter comes from a copy of that same Evolent guideline (last revised November 2024, implementation date July 2025) that I was able to locate. I am quoting only text that I actually retrieved from that document; anywhere I describe the guideline's content without a direct quotation, I say so explicitly. I ask Iowa Total Care/Evolent to confirm the exact edition of the guideline used to review my request and to identify any differences from the language below.

**1. The guideline's own "failure of conservative treatment" definition is satisfied**

The guideline defines the relevant fusion indication, in part, as requiring:

"Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months; NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment. Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute 'inability to complete' treatment."

My records document conservative treatment well beyond this six-week minimum, with no meaningful, durable improvement:

- **Symptom duration:** 24 months of progressive low back and leg pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised physical therapy:** 10 weeks (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-10), 20 completed visits, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, per the physical therapy discharge note. This is nearly double the six-week minimum referenced in the guideline.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection therapy:** Corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21, which produced only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned. [Please confirm with Dr. Reyes' office whether this injection was an epidural steroid injection or selective nerve root block, as the enclosed records do not specify the injection type.]
- **Current function despite this treatment:** I still cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, relieved only by sitting.

Under the guideline's own definition, this is a "[l]ack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment" — physical therapy, NSAIDs, and an injection have all been tried, each for a clinically appropriate duration, and my functional limitation (a 10-minute stand/walk tolerance) has not improved. This directly satisfies the conservative-treatment requirement quoted above, and it directly contradicts the stated reason for denial.

**2. The imaging findings meet the guideline's structural criteria for fusion**

The guideline further requires, for single-level fusion, "[i]maging studies corresponding to the clinical findings" and "[a]t least ONE of the following clinical conditions," including:

"Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, and congenital unilateral neural arch hypoplasia)"

My MRI of the lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs dated 2026-07-08 document grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension views, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. This is objective imaging evidence of degenerative spondylolisthesis with measurable segmental motion, corresponding directly to my clinical presentation of neurogenic claudication and radicular leg pain.

**3. Clinical picture as a whole**

On examination, I have neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, without bowel or bladder dysfunction. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke — none of which are contraindications to surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes (orthopedic surgery), has recommended lumbar fusion at L4-L5 based on this clinical and radiographic picture after conservative measures failed to provide lasting relief.

**Requested action**

Based on the above, I ask that Iowa Total Care/Evolent reverse the denial of CPT 22612 and approve the requested lumbar fusion. I have enclosed the following supporting records:

1. Physical therapy discharge note (10 weeks, 20 visits, 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-10)
2. Medication history documenting 6 months of NSAID use
3. Injection record dated 2026-03-21 and follow-up notes documenting 3 weeks of partial relief
4. MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiograph report, dated 2026-07-08
5. Physical examination/clinic notes documenting neurogenic claudication and diminished L5 sensation
6. Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes, MD [to be enclosed/attached]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome within the timeframe required by Iowa law and my plan documents. If any additional information is needed, please contact me at [Member Phone Number] or [Member Email]. If this appeal is denied, please identify the exact policy/guideline edition applied and explain how each unmet criterion was determined, and provide information on my right to further appeal, including any independent external review.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Emerson Jennings
Member ID: W359699103

Enclosures: as listed above
